My recommendation is (3) with one condition: the oracle keeps the report-only count of timer entries billed to a budget other than the one they interrupted (it is a few lines and makes the residual visible per case, as B24's nobody count does), so a later regression or a real B at more harts is seen. ### Architect · Answer

Event: `e29c0766befe56cc18e996fe9e8e93ef` · 2026-10-09T20:13:14Z

> Ruling: (3), drop B1 and `timer-any-hart`, with your condition and four more. Note: .wash/local/architect-questions.md, "SCHED3 B1".
> 
> Grounds. After A no gate line moves with B1 (deadline-flood 868,875/873,879 either way; exit-churn 577/596 against 571/603); its one effect is exit-churn rv64's 1229 entries, 31.7k ticks, 0.15 % of the pool; it has no failing negative; and it costs code on the switch path plus a section of deadline-notice latency. Tenet 1: deleting code beats carrying a feature nobody's target uses; Tenet 6: a mechanism without a negative is untested. The branch's B1 also departs from the ruling's form (global earliest + payer), so dropping it removes an unreviewed variant too.
> 
> What stays true. The gap is real in principle: a 1-thread victim cannot be repaid for billed work on its hart, and the placement that hides it now (91 of 96 destructions on the creator's own hart) is incidental, not proven attacker-proof. The 2-hart gates are its detectors; B1 stays in SCHED3-design.md as the known fix, not as code.
> 
> Conditions:
> 1. Yours: the oracle keeps a report-only count of timer entries billed to a budget other than the one they interrupted, with their ticks, per case, as B24's nobody count.
> 2. timer.md "R12 for timer work" states the residual with these numbers (exit-churn rv64 1229 / 31.7k, rv32 0; deadline-flood's placement); scheduling.md's residual risks point at it, since R12 is owned there. R12's promise text is unchanged.
> 3. deadline-flood's un-keep text records the placement, so a future failure with destructions on the victim's hart is read as a placement flip, not a new mechanism.
> 4. The B1-off notice latency (p99 4.6/5.1/4.6 ms rv64, 6.2/6.1/5.2 ms rv32) is the report's recorded baseline; the B1-on run need not finish.
> 5. Trigger, written in the design file: B1 returns as a plan node if the count's ticks reach 1 % of a victim's charged pool in any gate case, or a gate fails with destructions on the victim's hart.
